_note: DP1 serving-simulation HW catalog. Every number is {value, level, source, condition, rel_uncertainty, assumed}. Level A values are NOT stored here: they are loaded from measured/*.json produced by measure/ scripts and override the B entries with the same key (see hw.py:apply_measurements). Units: bytes, bytes/s, FLOP/s, seconds.

hbm_capacity_bytes.source: NVIDIA A100 datasheet (80GB HBM2e); 81920 MiB as reported by nvidia-smi

bf16_dense_flops.source: NVIDIA A100 datasheet: BF16 Tensor Core 312 TFLOPS dense (624 sparse)

host_link_bw_per_dir.source: PCIe Gen4 x16 = 32 GB/s/dir theoretical; pinned cudaMemcpy typically 24-26 GB/s

nvlink_bw_per_dir.source: NVLink bridge 600 GB/s bidirectional (2-GPU pairs only)

hbm_capacity_bytes.source: NVIDIA H100 SXM5 80GB HBM3; 81559 MiB as reported by nvidia-smi

bf16_dense_flops.source: NVIDIA H100 SXM datasheet: BF16 1,979 TFLOPS with sparsity -> 989 dense

host_link_bw_per_dir.source: PCIe Gen5 x16 = 64 GB/s/dir theoretical; pinned cudaMemcpy typically 45-55 GB/s

bf16_dense_flops.source: NVIDIA H100 PCIe datasheet: BF16 1,513 TFLOPS sparse -> 756 dense
same Hopper die as H100 SXM

hbm_capacity_bytes.source: NVIDIA HGX B200: 180 GB HBM3e per GPU (legacy configs/clusters.json used 192 GiB)

bf16_dense_flops.source: NVIDIA B200: BF16 4.5 PFLOPS sparse -> 2.25 dense

host_link_bw_per_dir.source: PCIe Gen5 x16 practical (Gen6 hosts would double this)

dram._role: Host DRAM reached over each GPU's PCIe link. The measurable HBM<->DRAM path of Phase 2/5.

capacity_bytes.source: placeholder 1 TiB; replaced by measure/00_env_check.sh MemTotal (A)

device_bw.source: DDR5-6400 x 8 channels = 409.6 GB/s per socket (JEDEC)

cxl_mem._role: CXL Type-3 memory expander (no compute). GPU reaches it through the CPU root complex, so GPU<->CXL = min(GPU PCIe link, sum of device BW).

devices.source: assumed 4 x8 expanders interleaved per socket

capacity_bytes.source: per device 256 GiB class (e.g. Samsung CMM-D 128/256 GB E3.S)

device_bw.source: Sun et al., 'Demystifying CXL Memory with Genuine CXL-Ready Systems and Devices', MICRO'23: ASIC CXL device (1ch DDR5-4800, 38.4 GB/s theor.) reaches a large fraction of its channel BW; FPGA devices substantially lower
device_bw.condition: Intel SPR host, sequential read, per device

latency_s.source: Sun et al. MICRO'23: CXL memory latency ~2.2x local 8-ch DDR5 (-> ~250 ns); Pond (ASPLOS'23) reports +70-90 ns over NUMA-local for direct-attached

cxl_pnm._role: CXL memory with near-memory compute (Samsung CXL-PNM class).

capacity_bytes.source: Park et al., 'An LPDDR-based CXL-PNM Platform for TCO-efficient Inference of Transformer-based LLMs', HPCA'24: 512 GB LPDDR5X

internal_bw.source: Park et al. HPCA'24: 1.1 TB/s. NOTE legacy configs/memories_default.json used 400 GB/s (DDR5-equivalent) - flagged discrepancy

device_bw.source: CXL 2.0/3.0 over PCIe Gen5 x16 = 64 GB/s/dir theoretical; ~80% efficiency assumed

compute_flops.source: user-provided FP32 1.64 TFLOPS x2 for FP16 (legacy config)

hbf._role: High Bandwidth Flash on the GPU package (UCIe). GPU-direct read, NAND write.

capacity_bytes.source: OCP HBF Technical Specification v1 (Sandisk + SK hynix, released 2026-08-03 at FMS 2026): up to 512 GB per package, 8-Hi/16-Hi NAND

read_bw.source: Sandisk HBF: Gen1 read up to 1.6 TB/s per stack; OCP spec grades 0.4-3.0 TB/s

write_bw.source: not in public spec; NAND program BW assumption (legacy config)

latency_s.source: not in public spec; NAND read ~us-class assumed

custom_hbm._role: User-defined memory node beside the GPU node (legacy DP1 design): 1 per domain, behind CPU over PCIe5 x16, attention-capable.

capacity_bytes.source: user rule: 2x paired GPU HBM capacity (legacy memories_default.json)

internal_bw.source: user rule: 2x paired GPU HBM BW

device_bw.source: PCIe Gen5 x16 practical, shared by whole domain

compute_flops.source: user rule: 20% of paired GPU dense FP16

device_bw.source: PCIe Gen4 enterprise NVMe seq read ~6.9-7 GB/s (e.g. Samsung PM9A3); Gen5 ~13-14 GB/s (e.g. PM1743)

llama_3_1_8b.source: HF config.json (B3). Fallback when only 1 GPU is available.

activation_reserve_bytes_per_gpu.source: profile_run peak activations + CUDA graphs; replaced by vLLM log 'Available KV cache memory' (A)

copy_interference.source: assumed step slowdown while a PCIe DMA is in flight; replaced by measure/01_transfer_microbench.py interference test (A)
